experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: 2-Acetoxynaphthalene; Typical Procedure. 2-Naphthol (1; 360 mg, 2.5 mmol) was treated with Ac2O (0.24 mL, 2.5 mmol) under neat conditions at r.t. for 15 min (monitored by GC-MS) under magnetic stirring in the presence of Cu(BF4)2·xH2O (5.92 mg, 0.025 mmol, 1 mol%). The reaction mixture was diluted with H2O (25 mL) and extracted with Et2O (3 × 15 mL). In most of the cases the products gave satisfactorily spectral (IR, 1H NMR and MS) data without any further purification. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for the preparation of N3- acylated dihydropyrimidines via anhydrides in highthroughput format (Scheme 2, Table 1). A mixture of 0.25 mmol of the corresponding DHPM 4A-J, 0.625 mmol (2.5 equiv.) of the corresponding anhydride, 0.625 mmol (2.5 equiv., 63 mg, 87 μL) of TEA, 0.05 mmol (0.2 equiv., 6.1 mg) of DMAP and 0.5 mL of anhydrous MeCN (HPLC Gradient Grade, dried over 3Å molecular sieves) is irradiated in a dry septum-capped 2.5 mL (small) microwave process vial with magnetic stirring in the microwave synthesizer for 5-20 min at 100-180 °C. After compressed gasjet cooling to ca. 35 °C (ca. 2 min) the vial is moved out of the cavity by the gripper and 2.5 mmol (45 mg, 45 μL) of water are added via syringe through the septum. The mixture is subsequently heated for an additional 5 min at 100 °C in the microwave cavity. After compressed gas-jet cooling to 35 °C (ca. 2 min) the solution is filtered through a standard 60×12 mm polypropylene frit. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for parallel synthesis of ureidothiophene carboxylic acid library: In a typical run, we realized the reactions with 8 thiaisatoic anhydrides A{1-19} and 10 amines B{1-60}. In a crystallizing dish intended to one selected amine, we disposed 1 mmole of each of the eight anhydrides in 8 glass jars. The addition of 2.2 mmoles of primary or secondary amines allowed the quick apparition of a solution. Magnetic stirring was pursued for 2 hours. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for parallel synthesis of ureidothiophene carboxylic acid library: In a typical run, we realized the reactions with 8 thiaisatoic anhydrides A{1-19} and 10 amines B{1-60}. In a crystallizing dish intended to one selected amine, we disposed 1 mmole of each of the eight anhydrides in 8 glass jars. Water (10 ml) was added to give an aqueous suspension of thiaisatoic anhydride and efficient magnetic stirring was performed. The addition of 2.2 mmoles of primary or secondary amines allowed the quick apparition of a solution. Magnetic stirring was pursued for 2 hours. About 5ml of a 37% hydrochloric acid solution were then added, the precipitate which was formed was filtered off and washed with water to give ureidothiophene carboxylic acids. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for catalyst recovery In a dry 250-mL, two-necked, round-bottomed flask was placed MoO2Cl2 (100 mg, 0.5 mmol) in 50 mL of anhydrous solvent (CH2Cl2 was used unless it is stated otherwise). To the above solution, anhydride (75 mmol) was slowly added at ambient temperature. After for 30 min, a solution of nucleophile (50 mmol in CH2Cl2, 20 mL) was slowly added to the above bluish solution and the reaction mixture was stirred for indicated time periods. After completion of the reaction as monitored by TLC, the reaction mixture was quenched with ice-cold water (100 mL). The separated aqueous layer was concentrated by rotatory evaporator at 40 °C. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for the preparation of N3- acylated dihydropyrimidines via anhydrides in highthroughput format (Scheme 2, Table 1). A mixture of 0.25 mmol of the corresponding DHPM 4A-J, 0.625 mmol (2.5 equiv.) of the corresponding anhydride, 0.625 mmol (2.5 equiv., 63 mg, 87 μL) of TEA, 0.05 mmol (0.2 equiv., 6.1 mg) of DMAP and 0.5 mL of anhydrous MeCN (HPLC Gradient Grade, dried over 3Å molecular sieves) is irradiated in a dry septum-capped 2.5 mL (small) microwave process vial with magnetic stirring in the microwave synthesizer for 5-20 min at 100-180 °C. After compressed gasjet cooling to ca. 35 °C (ca. 2 min) the vial is moved out of the cavity by the gripper and 2.5 mmol (45 mg, 45 μL) of water are added via syringe through the septum. The mixture is subsequently heated for an additional 5 min at 100 °C in the microwave cavity. After compressed gas-jet cooling to 35 °C (ca. 2 min) the solution is filtered through a standard 60×12 mm polypropylene frit. The SPE cartridge was prepared by filling the frit successively from the bottom with a 5 mm layer of silica gel 60, followed by a 5 mm pad of activated carbon and finally a 15 mm layer of a basic Al2O3/K2CO3 mixture (2:1). The desired N3- acylated DHPMs were eluted from the SPE cartridge with EtOAc (5 mL) applying either a mild vacuum or pressure. reference: Solution-phase parallel synthesis of a 1140-member ureidothiophene carboxylic acid library | Le Foulon, Francois-Xavier; Braud, Emmanuelle; Fabis, Frederic; Lancelot, Jean-Charles; Rault, Sylvain | Journal of Combinatorial Chemistry (2005), 7(2), 253-257
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for parallel synthesis of ureidothiophene carboxylic acid library: In a typical run, we realized the reactions with 8 thiaisatoic anhydrides A{1-19} and 10 amines B{1-60}. In a crystallizing dish intended to one selected amine, we disposed 1 mmole of each of the eight anhydrides in 8 glass jars. Water (10 ml) was added to give an aqueous suspension of thiaisatoic anhydride and efficient magnetic stirring was performed. The addition of 2.2 mmoles of primary or secondary amines allowed the quick apparition of a solution. Magnetic stirring was pursued for 2 hours. About 5ml of a 37% hydrochloric acid solution were then added, the precipitate which was formed was filtered off and washed with water to give ureidothiophene carboxylic acids. Analysis by 1H NMR and LC/MS identified successful reaction. Carbonylaminothiophene-2-carboxylic acid A7B2 Yield: 84%

title: Microwave-assisted scavenging of electrophiles utilizing polymer-supported sequestration reagents. Application to the synthesis of N3-acylated dihydropyrimidine libraries
authors: Dallinger, Doris; Gorobets, Nikolay Yu.; Kappe, C. Oliver
reference: Microwave-assisted scavenging of electrophiles utilizing polymer-supported sequestration reagents. Application to the synthesis of N3-acylated dihydropyrimidine libraries | Dallinger, Doris; Gorobets, Nikolay Yu.; Kappe, C. Oliver | Molecular Diversity (2003), 7(2-4), 229-245
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for the preparation of N3- acylated dihydropyrimidines via anhydrides in highthroughput format (Scheme 2, Table 1). A mixture of 0.25 mmol of the corresponding DHPM 4A-J, 0.625 mmol (2.5 equiv.) of the corresponding anhydride, 0.625 mmol (2.5 equiv., 63 mg, 87 μL) of TEA, 0.05 mmol (0.2 equiv., 6.1 mg) of DMAP and 0.5 mL of anhydrous MeCN (HPLC Gradient Grade, dried over 3Å molecular sieves) is irradiated in a dry septum-capped 2.5 mL (small) microwave process vial with magnetic stirring in the microwave synthesizer for 5-20 min at 100-180 °C. After compressed gasjet cooling to ca. 35 °C (ca. 2 min) the vial is moved out of the cavity by the gripper and 2.5 mmol (45 mg, 45 μL) of water are added via syringe through the septum. The mixture is subsequently heated for an additional 5 min at 100 °C in the microwave cavity. After compressed gas-jet cooling to 35 °C (ca. 2 min) the solution is filtered through a standard 60×12 mm polypropylene frit. The SPE cartridge was prepared by filling the frit successively from the bottom with a 5 mm layer of silica gel 60, followed by a 5 mm pad of activated carbon and finally a 15 mm layer of a basic Al2O3/K2CO3 mixture (2:1). The desired N3- acylated DHPMs were eluted from the SPE cartridge with EtOAc (5 mL) applying either a mild vacuum or pressure. Evaporation of the clear solution provided products as solids/oils in 32-99% yield and 81-99% purity. The chemical identity of all compounds was confirmed by 1H NMR and MS measurements (see below). Compound 5Ic, yield 98%. 1H NMR (DMSO-d6): δ 0.85 (t, J = 7.3 Hz, 3H), 1.07 (d, J = 6.5 Hz, 3H), 1.15-1.30 (m, 5H),1.45-1.59 (m, 2H), 2.21 (s, 3H), 2.68-2.72 and 2.84- 2.93 (2m, 2H), 4.09-4.14 (m, 2H), 5.25-5.32 (m, 1H), 10.00 (br s, 1H); MS (pos. APCI): m/z 283 (M+1).

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for parallel synthesis of ureidothiophene carboxylic acid library: In a typical run, we realized the reactions with 8 thiaisatoic anhydrides A{1-19} and 10 amines B{1-60}. In a crystallizing dish intended to one selected amine, we disposed 1 mmole of each of the eight anhydrides in 8 glass jars. Water (10 ml) was added to give an aqueous suspension of thiaisatoic anhydride and efficient magnetic stirring was performed. The addition of 2.2 mmoles of primary or secondary amines allowed the quick apparition of a solution. Magnetic stirring was pursued for 2 hours. About 5ml of a 37% hydrochloric acid solution were then added, the precipitate which was formed was filtered off and washed with water to give ureidothiophene carboxylic acids. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for parallel synthesis of ureidothiophene carboxylic acid library: In a typical run, we realized the reactions with 8 thiaisatoic anhydrides A{1-19} and 10 amines B{1-60}. In a crystallizing dish intended to one selected amine, we disposed 1 mmole of each of the eight anhydrides in 8 glass jars. Water (10 ml) was added to give an aqueous suspension of thiaisatoic anhydride and efficient magnetic stirring was performed. The addition of 2.2 mmoles of primary or secondary amines allowed the quick apparition of a solution. Magnetic stirring was pursued for 2 hours. About 5ml of a 37% hydrochloric acid solution were then added, the precipitate which was formed was filtered off and washed with water to give ureidothiophene carboxylic acids. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for parallel synthesis of ureidothiophene carboxylic acid library: In a typical run, we realized the reactions with 8 thiaisatoic anhydrides A{1-19} and 10 amines B{1-60}. In a crystallizing dish intended to one selected amine, we disposed 1 mmole of each of the eight anhydrides in 8 glass jars. Water (10 ml) was added to give an aqueous suspension of thiaisatoic anhydride and efficient magnetic stirring was performed. The addition of 2.2 mmoles of primary or secondary amines allowed the quick apparition of a solution. Magnetic stirring was pursued for 2 hours. About 5ml of a 37% hydrochloric acid solution were then added, the precipitate which was formed was filtered off and washed with water to give ureidothiophene carboxylic acids. Analysis by 1H NMR and LC/MS identified successful reaction. Carbonylaminothiophene-2-carboxylic acid A8B5 Yield: 84%

title: Solution-phase parallel synthesis of a 1140-member ureidothiophene carboxylic acid library
authors: Le Foulon, Francois-Xavier; Braud, Emmanuelle; Fabis, Frederic; Lancelot, Jean-Charles; Rault, Sylvain
reference: Solution-phase parallel synthesis of a 1140-member ureidothiophene carboxylic acid library | Le Foulon, Francois-Xavier; Braud, Emmanuelle; Fabis, Frederic; Lancelot, Jean-Charles; Rault, Sylvain | Journal of Combinatorial Chemistry (2005), 7(2), 253-257
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for parallel synthesis of ureidothiophene carboxylic acid library: In a typical run, we realized the reactions with 8 thiaisatoic anhydrides A{1-19} and 10 amines B{1-60}. In a crystallizing dish intended to one selected amine, we disposed 1 mmole of each of the eight anhydrides in 8 glass jars. Water (10 ml) was added to give an aqueous suspension of thiaisatoic anhydride and efficient magnetic stirring was performed. The addition of 2.2 mmoles of primary or secondary amines allowed the quick apparition of a solution. Magnetic stirring was pursued for 2 hours. About 5ml of a 37% hydrochloric acid solution were then added, the precipitate which was formed was filtered off and washed with water to give ureidothiophene carboxylic acids. Analysis by 1H NMR and LC/MS identified successful reaction. carbonylaminothiophene-2-carboxylic acid A4B7 Yield: 77%

title: Nucleophilic acyl substitutions of anhydrides with protic nucleophiles catalyzed by amphoteric, oxomolybdenum species
authors: Chen, Chien-Tien; Kuo, Jen-Huang; Pawar, Vijay D.; Munot, Yogesh S.; Weng, Shieu-Shien; Ku, Cheng-Hsiu; Liu, Cheng-Yuan
reference: Nucleophilic acyl substitutions of anhydrides with protic nucleophiles catalyzed by amphoteric, oxomolybdenum species | Chen, Chien-Tien; Kuo, Jen-Huang; Pawar, Vijay D.; Munot, Yogesh S.; Weng, Shieu-Shien; Ku, Cheng-Hsiu; Liu, Cheng-Yuan | Journal of Organic Chemistry (2005), 70(4), 1188-1197
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for acylation of tert-butanol and trityl alcohol In a dry 50-mL, two-necked, round-bottomed flask was placed MoO2Cl2 (19 mg, 0.1 mmol) in 5 mL of anhydrous toluene. A solution of anhydride (15 mmol) and a given 3o alcohol (10 mmol) in toluene (5 mL) was slowly added to the above solution and the reaction mixture was stirred for 30 min to 1 hour. To the above solution, diisopropylethylamine (1750 μL, 10 mmol) was slowly added at ambient temperature. This mixture was refluxed for 1 to 24 hours. After completion of the reaction as monitored by TLC (for the benzoylation of tryl alcohol), the reaction mixture was quenched with cold, saturated aqueous NaHCO3 solution (50 mL) at room temperature. The separated organic layer was washed with brine, dried (MgSO4), filtered, and evaporated. The crude product was purified by distillation. The product obtained was characterized by routine spectroscopic methods Benzyl-carbamic acid tert-butyl ester36 Data: 1H NMR (400 MHz, CDCl3) 7.34-7.23 (m, 5H), 5.01 (s, 1H), 4.30 (d, J = 5.5, 2H), 1.47 (s, 9H); 13C NMR (100 MHz, CDCl3) 155.82, 138.88, 128.34, 127.23, 127.02, 79.13, 44.42, 28.22; MS (ESI) 230 (M+Na+, 35), 181 (13); TLC Rf 0.43 (EtOAc/hexane, 1/10).

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for the preparation of N3- acylated dihydropyrimidines via anhydrides in highthroughput format (Scheme 2, Table 1). A mixture of 0.25 mmol of the corresponding DHPM 4A-J, 0.625 mmol (2.5 equiv.) of the corresponding anhydride, 0.625 mmol (2.5 equiv., 63 mg, 87 μL) of TEA, 0.05 mmol (0.2 equiv., 6.1 mg) of DMAP and 0.5 mL of anhydrous MeCN (HPLC Gradient Grade, dried over 3Å molecular sieves) is irradiated in a dry septum-capped 2.5 mL (small) microwave process vial with magnetic stirring in the microwave synthesizer for 5-20 min at 100-180 °C. After compressed gasjet cooling to ca. 35 °C (ca. 2 min) the vial is moved out of the cavity by the gripper and 2.5 mmol (45 mg, 45 μL) of water are added via syringe through the septum. The mixture is subsequently heated for an additional 5 min at 100 °C in the microwave cavity. After compressed gas-jet cooling to 35 °C (ca. 2 min) the solution is filtered through a standard 60×12 mm polypropylene frit. The SPE cartridge was prepared by filling the frit successively from the bottom with a 5 mm layer of silica gel 60, followed by a 5 mm pad of activated carbon and finally a 15 mm layer of a basic Al2O3/K2CO3 mixture (2:1). The desired N3- acylated DHPMs were eluted from the SPE cartridge with EtOAc (5 mL) applying either a mild vacuum or pressure. Evaporation of the clear solution provided products as solids/oils in 32-99% yield and 81-99% purity. The chemical identity of all compounds was confirmed by 1H NMR and MS measurements (see below). experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for parallel synthesis of ureidothiophene carboxylic acid library: In a typical run, we realized the reactions with 8 thiaisatoic anhydrides A{1-19} and 10 amines B{1-60}. In a crystallizing dish intended to one selected amine, we disposed 1 mmole of each of the eight anhydrides in 8 glass jars. Water (10 ml) was added to give an aqueous suspension of thiaisatoic anhydride and efficient magnetic stirring was performed. The addition of 2.2 mmoles of primary or secondary amines allowed the quick apparition of a solution. Magnetic stirring was pursued for 2 hours. reference: Solution-phase parallel synthesis of a 1140-member ureidothiophene carboxylic acid library | Le Foulon, Francois-Xavier; Braud, Emmanuelle; Fabis, Frederic; Lancelot, Jean-Charles; Rault, Sylvain | Journal of Combinatorial Chemistry (2005), 7(2), 253-257
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for parallel synthesis of ureidothiophene carboxylic acid library: In a typical run, we realized the reactions with 8 thiaisatoic anhydrides A{1-19} and 10 amines B{1-60}. In a crystallizing dish intended to one selected amine, we disposed 1 mmole of each of the eight anhydrides in 8 glass jars. Water (10 ml) was added to give an aqueous suspension of thiaisatoic anhydride and efficient magnetic stirring was performed. The addition of 2.2 mmoles of primary or secondary amines allowed the quick apparition of a solution. Magnetic stirring was pursued for 2 hours. About 5ml of a 37% hydrochloric acid solution were then added, the precipitate which was formed was filtered off and washed with water to give ureidothiophene carboxylic acids. Analysis by 1H NMR and LC/MS identified successful reaction. carbonylaminothiophene-2-carboxylic acid A2B5 Yield: 83%

reference: Microwave-assisted scavenging of electrophiles utilizing polymer-supported sequestration reagents. Application to the synthesis of N3-acylated dihydropyrimidine libraries | Dallinger, Doris; Gorobets, Nikolay Yu.; Kappe, C. Oliver | Molecular Diversity (2003), 7(2-4), 229-245
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for the preparation of N3- acylated dihydropyrimidines via anhydrides in highthroughput format (Scheme 2, Table 1). A mixture of 0.25 mmol of the corresponding DHPM 4A-J, 0.625 mmol (2.5 equiv.) of the corresponding anhydride, 0.625 mmol (2.5 equiv., 63 mg, 87 μL) of TEA, 0.05 mmol (0.2 equiv., 6.1 mg) of DMAP and 0.5 mL of anhydrous MeCN (HPLC Gradient Grade, dried over 3Å molecular sieves) is irradiated in a dry septum-capped 2.5 mL (small) microwave process vial with magnetic stirring in the microwave synthesizer for 5-20 min at 100-180 °C. After compressed gasjet cooling to ca. 35 °C (ca. 2 min) the vial is moved out of the cavity by the gripper and 2.5 mmol (45 mg, 45 μL) of water are added via syringe through the septum. The mixture is subsequently heated for an additional 5 min at 100 °C in the microwave cavity. After compressed gas-jet cooling to 35 °C (ca. 2 min) the solution is filtered through a standard 60×12 mm polypropylene frit. The SPE cartridge was prepared by filling the frit successively from the bottom with a 5 mm layer of silica gel 60, followed by a 5 mm pad of activated carbon and finally a 15 mm layer of a basic Al2O3/K2CO3 mixture (2:1). The desired N3- acylated DHPMs were eluted from the SPE cartridge with EtOAc (5 mL) applying either a mild vacuum or pressure. Evaporation of the clear solution provided products as solids/oils in 32-99% yield and 81-99% purity. The chemical identity of all compounds was confirmed by 1H NMR and MS measurements (see below). Compound 5Ec, yield 99% 1H NMR (DMSO-d6): δ 0.86 (t, J = 7.3 Hz, 3H), 1.28-1.32 (m, 2H), 1.46-1.67 (m, 2H), 2.56 (s, 3H), 2.65-2.74 and 2.93-3.02 (2m, 2H), 3.13 (s, 3H), 4.66 (s, 2H), 5.16-5.22 (m, 2H), 5.86-5.96 (m, 1H), 6.62 (s, 1H), 7.58-7.67 (m, 2H), 7.95 (s, 1H), 8.15 (d, J = 7.8 Hz, 1H); MS (pos. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for the preparation of N3- acylated dihydropyrimidines via anhydrides in highthroughput format (Scheme 2, Table 1). A mixture of 0.25 mmol of the corresponding DHPM 4A-J, 0.625 mmol (2.5 equiv.) of the corresponding anhydride, 0.625 mmol (2.5 equiv., 63 mg, 87 μL) of TEA, 0.05 mmol (0.2 equiv., 6.1 mg) of DMAP and 0.5 mL of anhydrous MeCN (HPLC Gradient Grade, dried over 3Å molecular sieves) is irradiated in a dry septum-capped 2.5 mL (small) microwave process vial with magnetic stirring in the microwave synthesizer for 5-20 min at 100-180 °C. After compressed gasjet cooling to ca. 35 °C (ca. 2 min) the vial is moved out of the cavity by the gripper and 2.5 mmol (45 mg, 45 μL) of water are added via syringe through the septum. The mixture is subsequently heated for an additional 5 min at 100 °C in the microwave cavity. After compressed gas-jet cooling to 35 °C (ca. 2 min) the solution is filtered through a standard 60×12 mm polypropylene frit. The SPE cartridge was prepared by filling the frit successively from the bottom with a 5 mm layer of silica gel 60, followed by a 5 mm pad of activated carbon and finally a 15 mm layer of a basic Al2O3/K2CO3 mixture (2:1). The desired N3- acylated DHPMs were eluted from the SPE cartridge with EtOAc (5 mL) applying either a mild vacuum or pressure. Evaporation of the clear solution provided products as solids/oils in 32-99% yield and 81-99% purity. The chemical identity of all compounds was confirmed by 1H NMR and MS measurements (see below). experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for parallel synthesis of ureidothiophene carboxylic acid library: In a typical run, we realized the reactions with 8 thiaisatoic anhydrides A{1-19} and 10 amines B{1-60}. In a crystallizing dish intended to one selected amine, we disposed 1 mmole of each of the eight anhydrides in 8 glass jars. Water (10 ml) was added to give an aqueous suspension of thiaisatoic anhydride and efficient magnetic stirring was performed. The addition of 2.2 mmoles of primary or secondary amines allowed the quick apparition of a solution. Magnetic stirring was pursued for 2 hours. About 5ml of a 37% hydrochloric acid solution were then added, the precipitate which was formed was filtered off and washed with water to give ureidothiophene carboxylic acids. reference: Solution-phase parallel synthesis of a 1140-member ureidothiophene carboxylic acid library | Le Foulon, Francois-Xavier; Braud, Emmanuelle; Fabis, Frederic; Lancelot, Jean-Charles; Rault, Sylvain | Journal of Combinatorial Chemistry (2005), 7(2), 253-257
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for parallel synthesis of ureidothiophene carboxylic acid library: In a typical run, we realized the reactions with 8 thiaisatoic anhydrides A{1-19} and 10 amines B{1-60}. In a crystallizing dish intended to one selected amine, we disposed 1 mmole of each of the eight anhydrides in 8 glass jars. Water (10 ml) was added to give an aqueous suspension of thiaisatoic anhydride and efficient magnetic stirring was performed. The addition of 2.2 mmoles of primary or secondary amines allowed the quick apparition of a solution. Magnetic stirring was pursued for 2 hours. About 5ml of a 37% hydrochloric acid solution were then added, the precipitate which was formed was filtered off and washed with water to give ureidothiophene carboxylic acids. Analysis by 1H NMR and LC/MS identified successful reaction. compd A14B50 m/z: 338.61 ESI+: 338.92 ESI-: 336.93

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: N,N-hexanoyltosylhydrazide (4): general procedure of acylation with an acid anhydride To a solution of N-tosylhydrazide 3 (50 mg, 0.27 mmol) in dichloromethane (1.3 mL) were added triethylamine (56 mL, 0.40 mmol) and 4-aminopyridine (5.0 mg, 0.40 mmol). The mixture was stirred for 30 min at 0 °C, quenched with sat. aq. solution of NaHCO3, and extracted with dichloromethane (5 mL x 2). title: Nucleophilic acyl substitutions of anhydrides with protic nucleophiles catalyzed by amphoteric, oxomolybdenum species
authors: Chen, Chien-Tien; Kuo, Jen-Huang; Pawar, Vijay D.; Munot, Yogesh S.; Weng, Shieu-Shien; Ku, Cheng-Hsiu; Liu, Cheng-Yuan
reference: Nucleophilic acyl substitutions of anhydrides with protic nucleophiles catalyzed by amphoteric, oxomolybdenum species | Chen, Chien-Tien; Kuo, Jen-Huang; Pawar, Vijay D.; Munot, Yogesh S.; Weng, Shieu-Shien; Ku, Cheng-Hsiu; Liu, Cheng-Yuan | Journal of Organic Chemistry (2005), 70(4), 1188-1197
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for acylation of tert-butanol and trityl alcohol In a dry 50-mL, two-necked, round-bottomed flask was placed MoO2Cl2 (19 mg, 0.1 mmol) in 5 mL of anhydrous toluene. A solution of anhydride (15 mmol) and a given 3o alcohol (10 mmol) in toluene (5 mL) was slowly added to the above solution and the reaction mixture was stirred for 30 min to 1 hour. To the above solution, diisopropylethylamine (1750 μL, 10 mmol) was slowly added at ambient temperature. This mixture was refluxed for 1 to 24 hours. After completion of the reaction as monitored by TLC (for the benzoylation of tryl alcohol), the reaction mixture was quenched with cold, saturated aqueous NaHCO3 solution (50 mL) at room temperature. The separated organic layer was washed with brine, dried (MgSO4), filtered, and evaporated. The crude product was purified by distillation. The product obtained was characterized by routine spectroscopic methods tert-Butyl-carbamic acid-tert-butyl ester41 Data: 1H NMR (400 MHz, CDCl3) 4.45 (bs, 1H), 1.42 (s, 9H), 1.28 (s, 9H); 13C NMR (100 MHz, CDCl3) 154.44, 78.43, 49.84, 28.93, 28.36; TLC Rf 0.40 (EtOAc/hexane, 1/4).

reference: Microwave-assisted scavenging of electrophiles utilizing polymer-supported sequestration reagents. Application to the synthesis of N3-acylated dihydropyrimidine libraries | Dallinger, Doris; Gorobets, Nikolay Yu.; Kappe, C. Oliver | Molecular Diversity (2003), 7(2-4), 229-245
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for the preparation of N3- acylated dihydropyrimidines via anhydrides in highthroughput format (Scheme 2, Table 1). A mixture of 0.25 mmol of the corresponding DHPM 4A-J, 0.625 mmol (2.5 equiv.) of the corresponding anhydride, 0.625 mmol (2.5 equiv., 63 mg, 87 μL) of TEA, 0.05 mmol (0.2 equiv., 6.1 mg) of DMAP and 0.5 mL of anhydrous MeCN (HPLC Gradient Grade, dried over 3Å molecular sieves) is irradiated in a dry septum-capped 2.5 mL (small) microwave process vial with magnetic stirring in the microwave synthesizer for 5-20 min at 100-180 °C. After compressed gasjet cooling to ca. 35 °C (ca. 2 min) the vial is moved out of the cavity by the gripper and 2.5 mmol (45 mg, 45 μL) of water are added via syringe through the septum. The mixture is subsequently heated for an additional 5 min at 100 °C in the microwave cavity. After compressed gas-jet cooling to 35 °C (ca. 2 min) the solution is filtered through a standard 60×12 mm polypropylene frit. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for parallel synthesis of ureidothiophene carboxylic acid library: In a typical run, we realized the reactions with 8 thiaisatoic anhydrides A{1-19} and 10 amines B{1-60}. In a crystallizing dish intended to one selected amine, we disposed 1 mmole of each of the eight anhydrides in 8 glass jars. Water (10 ml) was added to give an aqueous suspension of thiaisatoic anhydride and efficient magnetic stirring was performed. The addition of 2.2 mmoles of primary or secondary amines allowed the quick apparition of a solution. Magnetic stirring was pursued for 2 hours. About 5ml of a 37% hydrochloric acid solution were then added, the precipitate which was formed was filtered off and washed with water to give ureidothiophene carboxylic acids. authors: Dallinger, Doris; Gorobets, Nikolay Yu.; Kappe, C. Oliver
reference: Microwave-assisted scavenging of electrophiles utilizing polymer-supported sequestration reagents. Application to the synthesis of N3-acylated dihydropyrimidine libraries | Dallinger, Doris; Gorobets, Nikolay Yu.; Kappe, C. Oliver | Molecular Diversity (2003), 7(2-4), 229-245
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for the preparation of N3- acylated dihydropyrimidines via anhydrides in highthroughput format (Scheme 2, Table 1). A mixture of 0.25 mmol of the corresponding DHPM 4A-J, 0.625 mmol (2.5 equiv.) of the corresponding anhydride, 0.625 mmol (2.5 equiv., 63 mg, 87 μL) of TEA, 0.05 mmol (0.2 equiv., 6.1 mg) of DMAP and 0.5 mL of anhydrous MeCN (HPLC Gradient Grade, dried over 3Å molecular sieves) is irradiated in a dry septum-capped 2.5 mL (small) microwave process vial with magnetic stirring in the microwave synthesizer for 5-20 min at 100-180 °C. After compressed gasjet cooling to ca. 35 °C (ca. 2 min) the vial is moved out of the cavity by the gripper and 2.5 mmol (45 mg, 45 μL) of water are added via syringe through the septum. The mixture is subsequently heated for an additional 5 min at 100 °C in the microwave cavity. After compressed gas-jet cooling to 35 °C (ca. 2 min) the solution is filtered through a standard 60×12 mm polypropylene frit. The SPE cartridge was prepared by filling the frit successively from the bottom with a 5 mm layer of silica gel 60, followed by a 5 mm pad of activated carbon and finally a 15 mm layer of a basic Al2O3/K2CO3 mixture (2:1). The desired N3- acylated DHPMs were eluted from the SPE cartridge with EtOAc (5 mL) applying either a mild vacuum or pressure. Evaporation of the clear solution provided products as solids/oils in 32-99% yield and 81-99% purity. The chemical identity of all compounds was confirmed by 1H NMR and MS measurements (see below). experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for parallel synthesis of ureidothiophene carboxylic acid library: In a typical run, we realized the reactions with 8 thiaisatoic anhydrides A{1-19} and 10 amines B{1-60}. In a crystallizing dish intended to one selected amine, we disposed 1 mmole of each of the eight anhydrides in 8 glass jars. Water (10 ml) was added to give an aqueous suspension of thiaisatoic anhydride and efficient magnetic stirring was performed. The addition of 2.2 mmoles of primary or secondary amines allowed the quick apparition of a solution. Magnetic stirring was pursued for 2 hours. About 5ml of a 37% hydrochloric acid solution were then added, the precipitate which was formed was filtered off and washed with water to give ureidothiophene carboxylic acids. reference: Microwave-assisted scavenging of electrophiles utilizing polymer-supported sequestration reagents. Application to the synthesis of N3-acylated dihydropyrimidine libraries | Dallinger, Doris; Gorobets, Nikolay Yu.; Kappe, C. Oliver | Molecular Diversity (2003), 7(2-4), 229-245
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for the preparation of N3- acylated dihydropyrimidines via anhydrides in highthroughput format (Scheme 2, Table 1). A mixture of 0.25 mmol of the corresponding DHPM 4A-J, 0.625 mmol (2.5 equiv.) of the corresponding anhydride, 0.625 mmol (2.5 equiv., 63 mg, 87 μL) of TEA, 0.05 mmol (0.2 equiv., 6.1 mg) of DMAP and 0.5 mL of anhydrous MeCN (HPLC Gradient Grade, dried over 3Å molecular sieves) is irradiated in a dry septum-capped 2.5 mL (small) microwave process vial with magnetic stirring in the microwave synthesizer for 5-20 min at 100-180 °C. After compressed gasjet cooling to ca. 35 °C (ca. 2 min) the vial is moved out of the cavity by the gripper and 2.5 mmol (45 mg, 45 μL) of water are added via syringe through the septum. The mixture is subsequently heated for an additional 5 min at 100 °C in the microwave cavity. After compressed gas-jet cooling to 35 °C (ca. 2 min) the solution is filtered through a standard 60×12 mm polypropylene frit. The SPE cartridge was prepared by filling the frit successively from the bottom with a 5 mm layer of silica gel 60, followed by a 5 mm pad of activated carbon and finally a 15 mm layer of a basic Al2O3/K2CO3 mixture (2:1). The desired N3- acylated DHPMs were eluted from the SPE cartridge with EtOAc (5 mL) applying either a mild vacuum or pressure. Evaporation of the clear solution provided products as solids/oils in 32-99% yield and 81-99% purity. The chemical identity of all compounds was confirmed by 1H NMR and MS measurements (see below). Compound 5Cb, yield 74%. 1H NMR (DMSO-d6): δ 1.18 (t, J = 7.0 Hz, 3H), 2.39 (s, 3H), 4.14 (q, J = 7.0 Hz, 2H), 6.16 (s, 1H), 7.18 (m, 1H), 7.32 (m, 1H), 7.35-7.60 (m, 6H), 10.35 (s, 1H); MS (pos. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for parallel synthesis of ureidothiophene carboxylic acid library: In a typical run, we realized the reactions with 8 thiaisatoic anhydrides A{1-19} and 10 amines B{1-60}. In a crystallizing dish intended to one selected amine, we disposed 1 mmole of each of the eight anhydrides in 8 glass jars. Water (10 ml) was added to give an aqueous suspension of thiaisatoic anhydride and efficient magnetic stirring was performed. The addition of 2.2 mmoles of primary or secondary amines allowed the quick apparition of a solution. Magnetic stirring was pursued for 2 hours. About 5ml of a 37% hydrochloric acid solution were then added, the precipitate which was formed was filtered off and washed with water to give ureidothiophene carboxylic acids. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Preparation of N-Propanoyl Benzenesulfonamide: A Typical Procedure for N-Acylation of Sulfonamides in CH2Cl2 : A mixture of benzenesulfonamide (0.314 g, 2 mmol), propionyl chloride (0.184 g, 2 mmol) and P2O5/SiO2 [(w/w 75%), 0.35 g] was refluxed in CH2Cl2 (5 ml) for 60 min. A solution of anhydride (15 mmol) and a given 3o alcohol (10 mmol) in toluene (5 mL) was slowly added to the above solution and the reaction mixture was stirred for 30 min to 1 hour. To the above solution, diisopropylethylamine (1750 μL, 10 mmol) was slowly added at ambient temperature. This mixture was refluxed for 1 to 24 hours. After completion of the reaction as monitored by TLC (for the benzoylation of tryl alcohol), the reaction mixture was quenched with cold, saturated aqueous NaHCO3 solution (50 mL) at room temperature. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for parallel synthesis of ureidothiophene carboxylic acid library: In a typical run, we realized the reactions with 8 thiaisatoic anhydrides A{1-19} and 10 amines B{1-60}. In a crystallizing dish intended to one selected amine, we disposed 1 mmole of each of the eight anhydrides in 8 glass jars. Water (10 ml) was added to give an aqueous suspension of thiaisatoic anhydride and efficient magnetic stirring was performed. The addition of 2.2 mmoles of primary or secondary amines allowed the quick apparition of a solution. Magnetic stirring was pursued for 2 hours. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General Procedure for Products 3. To a mixture of anhydride 1 (1.0 mmol), tertiary amine 2 (0.5 mmol), and FeCl2 (1.6 mg, 0.0125 mmol), pyridine (40 μL, 0.5 mmol) and acetonitrile (3.0 mL) were added under nitrogen at room temperature. tert-Butyl hydroperoxide (70% aqueous solution, 136 μL, 1.0 mmol) was dropped into the mixture under nitrogen at room temperature. To the above solution, acyl anhydride (1.5 mmol) was slowly added at ambient temperature. After for 10 min, a solution of nucleophile (1.0 mmol in CH2Cl2, 2 mL) was slowly added to the above dark green solution and the reaction mixture was stirred for indicated time periods. After completion of the reaction as monitored by TLC, the reaction mixture was quenched with cold, saturated aqueous NaHCO3 solution (5 mL). For the acylation of β-hydroxy ketones or esters, ice-cold water was used to quench the reaction to prevent β-elimination. The separated organic layer was washed with brine, dried (MgSO4), filtered, and evaporated. The crude product was purified by column chromatography on silica gel if required (in most of the acetylation reactions, essentially pure material was obtained without further purification). experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for parallel synthesis of ureidothiophene carboxylic acid library: In a typical run, we realized the reactions with 8 thiaisatoic anhydrides A{1-19} and 10 amines B{1-60}. In a crystallizing dish intended to one selected amine, we disposed 1 mmole of each of the eight anhydrides in 8 glass jars. Water (10 ml) was added to give an aqueous suspension of thiaisatoic anhydride and efficient magnetic stirring was performed. The addition of 2.2 mmoles of primary or secondary amines allowed the quick apparition of a solution. Magnetic stirring was pursued for 2 hours. About 5ml of a 37% hydrochloric acid solution were then added, the precipitate which was formed was filtered off and washed with water to give ureidothiophene carboxylic acids. Analysis by 1H NMR and LC/MS identified successful reaction. compd A12B27 m/z: 332.17 ESI+: 332.94 ESI-: 330.98

authors: Dallinger, Doris; Gorobets, Nikolay Yu.; Kappe, C. Oliver
reference: Microwave-assisted scavenging of electrophiles utilizing polymer-supported sequestration reagents. Application to the synthesis of N3-acylated dihydropyrimidine libraries | Dallinger, Doris; Gorobets, Nikolay Yu.; Kappe, C. Oliver | Molecular Diversity (2003), 7(2-4), 229-245
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for the preparation of N3- acylated dihydropyrimidines via anhydrides in highthroughput format (Scheme 2, Table 1). A mixture of 0.25 mmol of the corresponding DHPM 4A-J, 0.625 mmol (2.5 equiv.) of the corresponding anhydride, 0.625 mmol (2.5 equiv., 63 mg, 87 μL) of TEA, 0.05 mmol (0.2 equiv., 6.1 mg) of DMAP and 0.5 mL of anhydrous MeCN (HPLC Gradient Grade, dried over 3Å molecular sieves) is irradiated in a dry septum-capped 2.5 mL (small) microwave process vial with magnetic stirring in the microwave synthesizer for 5-20 min at 100-180 °C. After compressed gasjet cooling to ca. 35 °C (ca. 2 min) the vial is moved out of the cavity by the gripper and 2.5 mmol (45 mg, 45 μL) of water are added via syringe through the septum. The mixture is subsequently heated for an additional 5 min at 100 °C in the microwave cavity. After compressed gas-jet cooling to 35 °C (ca. 2 min) the solution is filtered through a standard 60×12 mm polypropylene frit. The SPE cartridge was prepared by filling the frit successively from the bottom with a 5 mm layer of silica gel 60, followed by a 5 mm pad of activated carbon and finally a 15 mm layer of a basic Al2O3/K2CO3 mixture (2:1). The desired N3- acylated DHPMs were eluted from the SPE cartridge with EtOAc (5 mL) applying either a mild vacuum or pressure. Evaporation of the clear solution provided products as solids/oils in 32-99% yield and 81-99% purity. The chemical identity of all compounds was confirmed by 1H NMR and MS measurements (see below). Compound 5Ib, yield 79% 1H NMR (DMSO-d6): δ 1.18-1.32 (m, 6H), 2.29 (s, 3H), 4.15 (q, J = 7.0 Hz, 2H), 5.07 (d, J = 6.5 Hz, 1H), 7.36-7.45 (m, 2H), 7.45-7.54 (m, 3H); MS (pos. APCI): m/z 303 (M+1).

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: N,N-hexanoyltosylhydrazide (4): general procedure of acylation with an acid anhydride To a solution of N-tosylhydrazide 3 (50 mg, 0.27 mmol) in dichloromethane (1.3 mL) were added triethylamine (56 mL, 0.40 mmol) and 4-aminopyridine (5.0 mg, 0.40 mmol). experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for the preparation of N3- acylated dihydropyrimidines via anhydrides in highthroughput format (Scheme 2, Table 1). A mixture of 0.25 mmol of the corresponding DHPM 4A-J, 0.625 mmol (2.5 equiv.) of the corresponding anhydride, 0.625 mmol (2.5 equiv., 63 mg, 87 μL) of TEA, 0.05 mmol (0.2 equiv., 6.1 mg) of DMAP and 0.5 mL of anhydrous MeCN (HPLC Gradient Grade, dried over 3Å molecular sieves) is irradiated in a dry septum-capped 2.5 mL (small) microwave process vial with magnetic stirring in the microwave synthesizer for 5-20 min at 100-180 °C. After compressed gasjet cooling to ca. 35 °C (ca. 2 min) the vial is moved out of the cavity by the gripper and 2.5 mmol (45 mg, 45 μL) of water are added via syringe through the septum. The mixture is subsequently heated for an additional 5 min at 100 °C in the microwave cavity. After compressed gas-jet cooling to 35 °C (ca. 2 min) the solution is filtered through a standard 60×12 mm polypropylene frit. The desired N3- acylated DHPMs were eluted from the SPE cartridge with EtOAc (5 mL) applying either a mild vacuum or pressure. Evaporation of the clear solution provided products as solids/oils in 32-99% yield and 81-99% purity. The chemical identity of all compounds was confirmed by 1H NMR and MS measurements (see below). reference: Solution-phase parallel synthesis of a 1140-member ureidothiophene carboxylic acid library | Le Foulon, Francois-Xavier; Braud, Emmanuelle; Fabis, Frederic; Lancelot, Jean-Charles; Rault, Sylvain | Journal of Combinatorial Chemistry (2005), 7(2), 253-257
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for parallel synthesis of ureidothiophene carboxylic acid library: In a typical run, we realized the reactions with 8 thiaisatoic anhydrides A{1-19} and 10 amines B{1-60}. In a crystallizing dish intended to one selected amine, we disposed 1 mmole of each of the eight anhydrides in 8 glass jars. Water (10 ml) was added to give an aqueous suspension of thiaisatoic anhydride and efficient magnetic stirring was performed. The addition of 2.2 mmoles of primary or secondary amines allowed the quick apparition of a solution. Magnetic stirring was pursued for 2 hours. About 5ml of a 37% hydrochloric acid solution were then added, the precipitate which was formed was filtered off and washed with water to give ureidothiophene carboxylic acids. Analysis by 1H NMR and LC/MS identified successful reaction. compd: A2B56 m/z: 392.70 ESI+: 392.85 ESI-: 390.88
